title: Pain in Legs
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a middle-aged man with multiple cardiovascular risk factors — hypertension, hyperlipidemia, newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, and smoking — who presents with bilateral leg pain on exertion that is relieved by rest (intermittent claudication). He has diminished peripheral pulses and cool extremities. The ankle-brachial index is less than 0.7, consistent with moderate PAD (normal ≥ 1.0, claudication < 0.7, rest pain < 0.4). Importantly, he has intermittent claudication rather than rest pain, which means conservative management is appropriate rather than invasive intervention. The 6 P's of peripheral artery disease are: Pulselessness, Pain, Pallor, Poikilothermia, Paresthesia, and Paralysis.
chief_complaint: Bilateral leg pain on exertion, relieved by rest

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: Determine how sick the patient looks.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: Investigate for lung pathology.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Heart / Cardiovascular
stacks.finding: Cardiac pathology could cause leg pain — cardiovascular exam essential.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Extremities / Spine
stacks.finding: Chief complaint — examine extremities for pulses, skin changes, temperature.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych
stacks.finding: Neurological issues on differential for leg pain — neuro exam needed.

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: Good screening tool.

stacks.label: ECG, 12 lead
stacks.finding: Rule out cardiac causes of leg pain. PAD patients often have concomitant CAD.

stacks.label: Hemoglobin A1C, blood
stacks.finding: All patients with possible PVD should be evaluated for diabetes.

stacks.label: Lipid profile
stacks.finding: Lipids contribute to atherosclerosis — check and treat if abnormal. Goal LDL < 100 in PAD.

stacks.label: Microalbumin, urine (24-hour or spot)
stacks.finding: Newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes — screen for early glomerular disease.

stacks.label: Basic metabolic profile / Comprehensive metabolic profile / LFTs
stacks.finding: Chemistries are important screening tool.

stacks.label: Ankle-brachial index / Arterial Doppler, lower extremities
stacks.finding: ABI is the main diagnostic tool. ABI < 0.7 = claudication. Normal ≥ 1.0. Non-invasive, first-line.

stacks.label: Angiography, lower extremity
stacks.finding: Invasive test with contrast risks. Conservative management first for intermittent claudication, not rest pain.

stacks.label: Metformin
stacks.finding: First-line therapy for type 2 diabetes. Start at diagnosis.

stacks.label: ACE inhibitor (Lisinopril / Enalapril / Ramipril) or ARB
stacks.finding: ACE inhibitors are first-line for hypertensive diabetics — nephroprotective. ARB if ACEI intolerant.

stacks.label: Statin (Atorvastatin / Rosuvastatin / Simvastatin)
stacks.finding: Statin for hyperlipidemia — prevents worsening of PVD. Goal LDL < 100 mg/dL.

stacks.label: Aspirin, therapy
stacks.finding: Antiplatelet therapy indicated for PAD. Aspirin is most common and most tested. Reduces cardiovascular events.

stacks.label: Instruct patient, smoking cessation
stacks.finding: One of the most important interventions — smoking accelerates PVD.

stacks.label: Diet modification (calorie-restricted / diabetic / DASH)
stacks.finding: Weight loss to control diabetes and hypertension. DASH diet for hypertension.

stacks.label: Instruct patient, diabetes
stacks.finding: Diabetes education increases compliance and improves outcomes.

stacks.label: Advise patient, exercise program
stacks.finding: Exercise is excellent for weight loss, glucose control, and collateral circulation development. Supervised walking programs improve claudication symptoms.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Diminished peripheral pulses. Assess for bruits (carotid, femoral). Hypertension.
physical_exam.neurological: Rule out neurogenic claudication (spinal stenosis) vs vascular claudication. Vascular: pain with exertion, relieved quickly by rest. Neurogenic: pain with standing/walking, relieved by sitting/leaning forward.

decoys.label: Angiography / Arteriography
decoys.reason_wrong: Invasive, uses contrast (nephrotoxic, allergic reactions), expensive. Conservative management with risk factor modification is first-line for intermittent claudication. Only for rest pain or failed medical therapy.

decoys.label: Surgical bypass / Angioplasty
decoys.reason_wrong: Not indicated for intermittent claudication. Reserved for rest pain, tissue loss, or disabling symptoms refractory to conservative therapy.

decoys.label: CT angiography
decoys.reason_wrong: Radiation + iodinated contrast exposure. Duplex ultrasound or ABI is preferred non-invasive screening.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: ABI is the gold standard screening test. Normal ≥ 1.0. Claudication < 0.7. Rest pain < 0.4. Non-invasive, reproducible.
Intermittent claudication without rest pain = conservative therapy. Risk factor modification: smoking cessation, exercise, diet, medication optimization.
Aspirin reduces cardiovascular events. Statin lowers LDL to < 100. ACEI/ARB is nephroprotective in diabetes and controls hypertension.
New T2DM — metformin first-line. Diabetes education, calorie-restricted diet, exercise program. Control of glucose slows vascular disease progression.
Arteriography is invasive with contrast risks. Reserved for failed conservative therapy or rest pain requiring revascularization.

case_summary: PAD with intermittent claudication. Multiple risk factors: HTN, HLD, DM2, smoking. ABI < 0.7 confirms. Conservative management: aspirin, statin, ACEI, metformin, smoking cessation, diet, exercise. Avoid invasive angiography. Follow-up in 7 days. Prognosis: good with risk factor control.
